---

The CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts are frozen once per week by the
`/forecast-capture` skill, which snapshots predictions **before kickoff** and reports what
moved since the prior week.

## Scope and entry point (changed 2026-09-02, per Eric)

- **All 16 Big 12 teams every week**, not Baylor only. The list is the `BIG12` constant in
  `weekly_capture.py` — one home; do not copy team lists into the wrapper or the skill.
  `--teams`/`--team` still narrow a run. Budget ~10 min for the full sweep.
- **One entry point:** `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh` (capture → compare
  `--all --archive`). It hardcodes the absolute `uv` path.
- **Archive mirror:** every snapshot and comparison is copied to
  `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`. Read-only copy; truth stays in
  `CFB_Victory_Model/data/`. Registered in `backup-manifest.json` as `personal`/ssd —
  see [[backup-sync-system]] for why a new `~/DEV` folder must be added there.
- The ritual guard still keys off the newest `*_baylor.csv`, which the Big 12 sweep always
  writes, so detection is unaffected.

## A gap can mean the other machine captured it

Confirmed 2026-09-09. The Mac's `data/weekly_forecast_log.csv` looked like it had
missed 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-31 — it jumped 07-31 → 09-02. Neither week was
missed. **Both were captured on the Windows box**, which runs the same wrapper
against the same repo. The two machines had diverged, each holding captures the
other lacked.

Before declaring a missed week, check the other machine's copy of the log.
Merging is safe: the natural key is `(captured_at, season, team, week, game_id)`,
and a union on that key had **zero conflicts** across 216 Mac + 348 Windows rows
→ 540. Same key never carried different values. See [[github-consolidation]].

**Superseded 2026-10-24:** the capture now runs on the Mac only. The Windows laptop has had no
terminal work or jobs since 2026-10-14 (desktop-app only since 10-21). Check the Windows copy
only for weeks before then; a later gap is a real gap.

## An old newest-snapshot file is not proof of a missed week

Checked 2026-09-02: the newest snapshot was `2026-07-31_baylor.csv`, and both the skill and
COMMANDS.md asserted the 08-24 and 08-31 weeks were "gone for good". They were not — Baylor's
opener was 2026-09-05, so no game had been played and nothing had been overwritten. **A week
is lost only if a game was actually played inside the gap.** Verify before declaring a loss:

```
curl -s "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/college-football/teams/239/schedule?season=2026"
```

(239 = Baylor; read each event's `status.type.name`.) Both docs were corrected.

## Cadence

- ~~**Wednesdays**, season window **2026-08-26 → 2027-01-20**~~ — superseded
  2026-08-15. Current cadence is **Monday-anchored**, season window
  **2026-08-24 → 2027-01-23**. Capture day: ideally Wednesday; Thursday or Friday works while no Big 12 game has kicked off (`~/.claude/skills/forecast-capture/SKILL.md`, the authority; 2026-11-02).

## "Nothing moved" in season = dead report link (2026-10-23)

The site swapped to a new Power BI report around 10-05. `REPORT` in `weekly_capture.py` still
opened the old one, which kept loading with no error but froze at ~10-02. Three captures
(10-07, 10-14, 10-23) were copies; a session wrongly told Eric the *site* was stale, and Eric
corrected it (the site was current). Week 6-7 pre-game forecasts are lost. Fix: compare `REPORT`
with the iframe on `cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/`. Also in the repo's STATUS Gotchas.

## The constraint that makes the cadence non-negotiable

**There is no backfill.** A pre-game forecast is only capturable before the game is played;
a missed week is permanently missing from the series, not a chore that rolls
forward. This is why the reminder escalates rather than silently re-queuing.

## Mac-side guard (built 2026-08-15)

`ritual-check.ps1` now carries a fourth ritual, `forecast-capture`, so the cadence is
enforced on this machine rather than depending on memory (enforced only while the rituals
timer ran; see "Superseded 2026-10-24" under Schedule below). It detects captures from the
artifact itself — newest `*_baylor.csv` in `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots/`
— matching the script's existing "the artifact is the record, not a state file" rule.

**The real deadline is Saturday's kickoffs, not a maintenance window.** The report
overwrites its Chance of Victory column with the realised result once a game is *played* —
that is what destroyed 2019–2025. Nothing scheduled updates midweek.

Cadence (Monday-anchored, per Eric 2026-08-15 — he wanted the warning early in the week):
**Mon DUE → Tue–Sat OVERDUE → Sun silent** (games played, week gone). Season bounds are the
Monday of the opening week (2026-08-24) and the Saturday of the closing week (2027-01-23),
widened from the documented 08-26 → 01-20 so neither end truncates a live capture window.

A third status, **RECHECK**, exists because an early capture is not proof of a good one: the
source may not have refreshed the coming weekend's numbers on Monday, so a Monday snapshot
can hold last week's figures. Treating "captured this week" as done would let a stale
snapshot pass for a good week — the exact risk that makes capturing early otherwise unsafe.
So a capture taken *earlier* in the week keeps surfacing through Wednesday. Capturing today
always satisfies today; RECHECK means *verify*, not *you missed it*.

Three counterintuitive silences (off-season, Sunday, post-Wednesday-once-captured) plus the
RECHECK window are pinned by `tests/keystone-ritual-forecast-capture.ps1`. Both a
days-since-last-capture and a naive "captured this week → OK" implementation fail them. The
script gained `-Today` and `-CfbSnapshotDir` seams to make this testable.

**`-Notify` was mute on this Mac from the migration until 2026-08-15** — it shelled out to
`msg.exe` (Windows-only), so every scheduled run hit the catch and logged "desktop prompt
unavailable" where nobody reads it. Now `osascript`, dialog with a banner fallback. This
affected *all* rituals, which is consistent with interview-me sitting 12 days overdue and
weekly-review 15. If ritual nags ever go quiet again, test `-Notify` directly before
assuming the rituals are simply current.

Schedule: `com.keystone.rituals` fires Mon–Fri 17:00 plus Fri 15:30, so Monday's DUE and the
Tue–Fri escalation all land. **Saturday and Sunday have no trigger** — Saturday's OVERDUE is
therefore only visible if the script is run by hand. Acceptable because Fri 15:30 and 17:00
are the last useful warnings anyway, but it does mean the Saturday branch is effectively a
manual-run safety net, not a live alarm.

**Superseded 2026-10-24 — nothing nags any more.** `com.keystone.rituals` has been disabled
since 2026-09-24, so none of the triggers above fire. `ritual-check.ps1` still runs daily at
06:00 inside `com.keystone.morning` (`morning-cadence.ps1`), without `-Notify`: the
forecast-capture DUE/OVERDUE shows only in `KeystoneOS/outputs/morning/cadence.log`. In season
the capture depends on someone running `/forecast-capture`. See [[automation-cadence]].

A Windows-side scheduled task `CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder` was left enabled when the
Windows box was retired 2026-08-14 — it operates under that machine's own `~/Desktop/DEV`
and touches none of the Mac repos, so it is harmless but is *not* the authoritative
reminder. See [[backup-sync-system]]. **Superseded 2026-10-24:** all Windows scheduled tasks
were disabled 2026-10-08, and the 2026-10-23 audit found this one is dead code (it calls the
archived morning-briefing package). See [[automation-cadence]] and [[work-laptop-hands-off]].

Related model/data work lives in [[cfb-analytics-lab]] (a separate project —
`~/DEV/CFB_Analytics_Lab` vs the Victory Model's own tree).

## Evaluation and the market line (2026-10-30)

- **Late capture check for all 16 teams in one call:** the ESPN scoreboard with the Big 12
  group, one date at a time (a date range returned nothing):
  `curl -s "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/college-football/scoreboard?groups=4&dates=YYYYMMDD&limit=100"`.
  A Friday capture is safe if no Big 12 game was played Thursday.
- **The opening betting line beat the model** on the first 68 true pregame games (winners 76% vs
  81%, margin miss 12.9 vs 11.4). A Codex audit found no correction to the model's numbers with
  a clear gain. So `weekly_run.sh` now also prints model vs opening line (`market_view.py`).
- **REA does not apply:** there is no binary, only Garrett's published Power BI report. The
  model's structure was recovered from its outputs instead (in the repo's STATUS).
- Details: `EVAL_2026_SEASON.md`, `docs/MODEL_AUDIT_2026-10-30.md` in the repo.

---RUN
#!/bin/bash
# Weekly CFB Victory Model freeze - all 16 Big 12 teams, then the comparison.
#
# Run it Wednesday of a game week. A Chrome window opens; that is required, not
# a bug. Headless breaks the Power BI team slicer.
#
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh                       # all Big 12, 2026
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams Baylor TCU    # just these two
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --year 2027
#
# Snapshots land in data/weekly_snapshots/ and are copied to
# ../CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/ along with each team's comparison text.
set -euo pipefail

# Background/launchd shells get a minimal PATH, so nothing here relies on it.
UV=/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Without this, Python block-buffers stdout whenever the run is redirected to a
# file, so a 10-minute run shows nothing until it finishes.
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Capture exits non-zero if any team failed both passes. Skip the comparison
# then: it diffs whatever snapshots are newest, so after a failed capture it
# prints last week's numbers as if they were today's. Captures are idempotent,
# so fix the cause and re-run (or --teams <the failed ones>).
echo "=== capture ==="
rc=0
"$UV" run --with playwright python weekly_capture.py "$@" || rc=$?

if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo
    echo "=== comparison SKIPPED: capture failed (exit $rc) ==="
    echo "Fix the error above and re-run the failed teams. Teams that succeeded are saved; nothing was compared."
    exit "$rc"
fi

echo
echo "=== comparison ==="
"$UV" run python compare_snapshots.py --all --archive

# Opening lines for the coming games. cfbd_pull.py skips files that exist, so
# move last week's file aside and put it back if the pull fails. A failure here
# never fails the run: the capture above is the part that cannot be redone.
echo
echo "=== model vs opening line ==="
LINES=data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv
[ -f "$LINES" ] && mv "$LINES" "$LINES.prev"
if "$UV" run python cfbd_pull.py --years 2026 --only lines >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$LINES" ]; then
    rm -f "$LINES.prev"
    "$UV" run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python market_view.py || echo "market view failed"
else

#!/bin/bash
# Weekly CFB Victory Model freeze - all 16 Big 12 teams, then the comparison.
#
# Run it Wednesday of a game week. A Chrome window opens; that is required, not
# a bug. Headless breaks the Power BI team slicer.
#
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh                       # all Big 12, 2026
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams Baylor TCU    # just these two
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --year 2027
#
# Snapshots land in data/weekly_snapshots/ and are copied to
# ../CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/ along with each team's comparison text.
set -euo pipefail

# Background/launchd shells get a minimal PATH, so nothing here relies on it.
UV=/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Without this, Python block-buffers stdout whenever the run is redirected to a
# file, so a 10-minute run shows nothing until it finishes.
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Capture exits non-zero if any team failed both passes. Skip the comparison
# then: it diffs whatever snapshots are newest, so after a failed capture it
# prints last week's numbers as if they were today's. Captures are idempotent,
# so fix the cause and re-run (or --teams <the failed ones>).
echo "=== capture ==="
rc=0
"$UV" run --with playwright python weekly_capture.py "$@" || rc=$?

if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo
    echo "=== comparison SKIPPED: capture failed (exit $rc) ==="
    echo "Fix the error above and re-run the failed teams. Teams that succeeded are saved; nothing was compared."
    exit "$rc"
fi

echo
echo "=== comparison ==="
"$UV" run python compare_snapshots.py --all --archive

# Opening lines for the coming games. cfbd_pull.py skips files that exist, so
# move last week's file aside and put it back if the pull fails. A failure here
# never fails the run: the capture above is the part that cannot be redone.
echo
echo "=== model vs opening line ==="
LINES=data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv
[ -f "$LINES" ] && mv "$LINES" "$LINES.prev"
if "$UV" run python cfbd_pull.py --years 2026 --only lines >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$LINES" ]; then
    rm -f "$LINES.prev"
    "$UV" run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python market_view.py || echo "market view failed"
else
    [ -f "$LINES.prev" ] && mv "$LINES.prev" "$LINES"
    echo "CFBD line pull failed; skipped. The capture and comparison above are fine."
fi

exit $rc

# Text Eric's phone through the Mac's Messages app (iMessage). Mac only.
# Usage: ~/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh "message"

on run argv
  tell application "Messages"
    set svc to 1st account whose service type = iMessage
    send (item 2 of argv) to participant (item 1 of argv) of svc
  end tell
end run
OSA

#!/bin/bash
# Unattended weekly capture, run by launchd (ops/com.keystone.forecastcapture.plist):
# Wed 10:40, plus a Thu 10:40 backup run. It wraps weekly_run.sh, then texts Eric one line.
#
#   scripts/scheduled_capture.sh                  # what launchd runs
#   FORCE=1 scripts/scheduled_capture.sh --teams Baylor   # test: skip the date checks
#
# It does NOT do the skill's human checks (gap audit, ESPN kickoff check) or the
# report; ask Claude for /forecast-capture to read the result. It does not commit.
set -uo pipefail

UV=/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv
TEXT=/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh
ALERT_LOG=/Users/kristinarash/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
SNAP="$ROOT/data/weekly_snapshots"
TODAY=$(date +%F)
LOG="$ROOT/logs/scheduled-capture-$TODAY.log"
mkdir -p "$ROOT/logs"

say() { "$TEXT" "$1" >> "$LOG" 2>&1 || echo "text failed" >> "$LOG"; }
alert() { printf '[%s] forecast-capture: %s (log: %s)\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$1" "$LOG" >> "$ALERT_LOG"; }

if [ "${FORCE:-0}" != 1 ]; then
    # Season window, from the cfb-forecast-capture memory (Monday-anchored cadence).
    if [[ "$TODAY" < 2026-08-24 || "$TODAY" > 2027-01-23 ]]; then exit 0; fi
    # Skip if a capture already exists from Tuesday of this week on. A Monday capture
    # does not count: the site may not have refreshed yet (the RECHECK rule).
    n=$(( $(date +%u) - 2 ))   # days since Tuesday (%u: 1 = Monday)
    if [ "$n" -ge 0 ]; then tue=$(date -v-"${n}"d +%F); else tue=$(date -v+"$(( -n ))"d +%F); fi
    newest=$(ls "$SNAP" | grep '_baylor\.csv$' | sort | tail -1 | cut -c1-10)
    if [[ ! "$newest" < "$tue" ]]; then
        echo "[$TODAY] skipped: already captured $newest" >> "$LOG"; exit 0
    fi
fi

{
    echo "=== scheduled capture $(date '+%F %T') ==="
    # A playwright update needs a new Chromium; without it, both runs die the same way.
    "$UV" run --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium
    "$ROOT/scripts/weekly_run.sh" "$@"
} >> "$LOG" 2>&1
rc=$?

teams=$(ls "$SNAP" | grep -c "^${TODAY}_")
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    msg="CFB forecast capture FAILED (exit $rc, $teams teams saved). Action: ask Claude to run /forecast-capture before any Big 12 kickoff."
    alert "FAILED exit $rc"
elif grep -q "No game was newly played and no forecast moved" "$LOG"; then
    msg="CFB forecast captured ($teams teams), but nothing moved. The report link may be dead. Action: ask Claude for /forecast-capture step 5."
    alert "nothing moved: report link may be dead"
else
    msg="CFB forecast captured, $teams teams. No action needed. Ask Claude for the /forecast-capture report when you want it."
fi
echo "$msg" >> "$LOG"
say "$msg"
exit "$rc"

---
name: forecast-capture
description: >-
  Freeze the CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts for all 16 Big 12 teams before
  kickoff, then report what moved since the last capture. Use for "/forecast-capture",
  "capture the CFB forecast", or "did we capture this week". Do not use for live
  scores, standings, or schedules (use pp-espn).
---

# Forecast Capture

The report at cfbvictorymodel.com **overwrites each game's Chance of Victory
with the result once the game is played**. That erased every pre-game forecast
from 2019 to 2025. This skill freezes the forecasts once per game week, so 2026
is the first season that can be graded. A forecast exists only until kickoff:
there is no backfill.

Run it on the Mac, from the main checkout `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model`, ideally
**Wednesday** of a game week (after the model has taken in the weekend, before
any Thursday game). Thursday or Friday works while no Big 12 game has kicked off.
Takes no arguments.

## Steps

1. **Find the last capture.**
   `ls ~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots/ | tail -16`
   All 16 should share the newest date; a team missing from it failed last
   time and its gap runs from its own newest file. A gap of 8+ days *may* mean a lost week. A week is lost only if a Big 12
   game was played inside the gap with no capture before it; confirm with
   step 2's scoreboard query on the gap's game days before calling it lost.

2. **Check nothing this week has kicked off.** For each day from Thursday of
   this game week through today:
   `curl -s "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/college-football/scoreboard?groups=4&dates=YYYYMMDD&limit=100"`
   (`groups=4` is the Big 12; one date per call, a range returns nothing.) A
   game whose `status.type.name` is anything but `STATUS_SCHEDULED` has
   kicked off. Its forecast is lost only if neither team has a snapshot dated
   after last weekend and before that kickoff; name every lost game in the
   report.

3. **Run the wrapper.** It is the one route; read it for what it runs.
   `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh`
   It captures all 16 teams, compares with the last capture, archives both to
   `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`, then prints model vs opening line.
   A Chrome window opens: the capture runs headed by design, because headless
   Power BI never renders most of the team list. Budget ~10 minutes.
   `Team attempt 1 failed, retrying...` is normal start-up racing.

4. **Read the capture result.** Success is exit 0 and no `FAILED for:` line.
   On failure the wrapper prints `comparison SKIPPED` and compares nothing.
   Fix the cause and re-run the failed teams only:
   `scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams <failed teams>`. Re-running the same day is
   safe: it replaces that day's snapshot and log rows. Error fixes are in
   [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md).

5. **Check the report link is live.** After a game weekend, the comparison
   must show games newly played. If it prints
   `No game was newly played and no forecast moved.` (in a single-team run:
   `No material change`), treat it as a **dead report link**, not a quiet
   week: the site swapped its Power BI report around 10-05, the old link kept
   loading frozen data with no error, and weeks 6-7 were lost that way. Open
   https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/ in a browser, compare
   the iframe's `view?r=` key with `REPORT` in `weekly_capture.py`, update
   `REPORT` if they differ, and re-run step 3. (Plain `curl` of that page got
   HTTP 406 on 2026-10-31.)

6. **Report back**, short. Lead with how many of 16 teams captured, then the
   rollup table (team, exp wins, change, played, moved). Then:
   1. **Games played since last capture**: side correct/wrong and margin miss,
      from each team's `GAMES PLAYED SINCE LAST CAPTURE` block. This track
      record is the point of the whole project.
   2. **Forecasts that moved**: which games and by how much. A big swing
      usually means the model re-rated an opponent after its weekend.
   3. **Season outlook drift**: expected wins now vs last capture.
   4. **Model vs opening line**: name every `CHECK` game (15+ point gap; the
      line was the better 2026 forecast, `docs/MODEL_AUDIT_2026-10-30.md`).
      If the wrapper printed `CFBD line pull failed` or `market view failed`,
      say the table is missing.
   5. **Anomalies and losses**: a `NEW GAME` line, a team with fewer than 12
      `games` (the comparison never names a vanished game, so a lower count is
      the only sign), a wild swing, and every lost week or game from steps 1-2.

**Done when** the wrapper exited 0 with 16 snapshots dated today, step 5 showed
games newly played (or the scoreboard confirms no Big 12 game since the last
capture, or `REPORT` was fixed and the capture re-run), and the
report covers all five items, with every lost game named.

## Scope

All 16 Big 12 teams, every week. The list has one home: `BIG12` in
`weekly_capture.py`; edit it there if the conference changes. One full run per
game week keeps the load light on a one-person hobby server; teams outside the
Big 12 only on request (see [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md)).

name: brew-git-keychain-hang
description: "After a brew git upgrade, git to GitHub hung on a Keychain prompt; git now signs in through gh (2026-10-25)"
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-10-25 a Homebrew upgrade of git made every git pull and push to GitHub hang on 'git credential-osxkeychain get' (macOS Keychain dialog for the new ad-hoc-signed helper). Fixed with 'gh auth setup-git': github.com and gist.github.com now use gh as the credential helper.

**Why:** brew ships an ad-hoc-signed git-credential-osxkeychain, so each new build triggers a Keychain allow-access dialog; pulls, pushes, autopush and the backup wait on it silently.

**How to apply:** If git to GitHub hangs after a brew upgrade, look in ps for 'git credential-osxkeychain get', and check that 'git config --global --get-regexp credential' still sends github.com to '!/opt/homebrew/bin/gh auth git-credential'. gh reads its token through Apple's /usr/bin/security, so it does not prompt after upgrades. Old ~/.gitconfig: ~/.claude/backups/gitconfig.pre-gh-helper-2026-10-25. Related: brew openssl@3 now tracks the 3.5 LTS (3.6.4 -> 3.5.9 looks like a downgrade but is intended) and rebuilds node and python@3.14; DEV venvs use /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14, so patch upgrades do not break them. See [[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]], [[pwsh-launchd-wrapper-trap]].

new_head='''# It runs headless (no window); if that fails it re-runs headed (captures are
# idempotent). Then it commits and pushes the snapshots and log (Eric approved
# unattended push, 2026-11-02). It does NOT do the skill's human checks (gap audit,
# ESPN kickoff check) or the report; ask Claude for /forecast-capture for those.'''

old_run='''{
    echo "=== scheduled capture $(date '+%F %T') ==="

    "$UV" run --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium
    "$ROOT/scripts/weekly_run.sh" "$@"
} >> "$LOG" 2>&1
rc=$?
'''
new_run='''{
    echo "=== scheduled capture $(date '+%F %T') ==="
    # A playwright update needs a new Chromium; without it, both runs die the same way.
    "$UV" run --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium
    "$ROOT/scripts/weekly_run.sh" --headless "$@"
} >> "$LOG" 2>&1
rc=$?
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "=== headless failed (exit $rc); re-running headed $(date '+%F %T') ===" >> "$LOG"
    "$ROOT/scripts/weekly_run.sh" "$@" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
    rc=$?
fi

# Commit only the frozen forecasts, never other work in the tree, then push.
DATA=(data/weekly_snapshots data/weekly_forecast_log.csv)
push_bg() {  # git push can hang on a credential prompt; give it 90 s
    git push -q >> "$LOG" 2>&1 & local pid=$!
    for _ in $(seq 1 90); do kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || { wait "$pid"; return $?; }; sleep 1; done
    kill "$pid"; return 124
}
git_note="Nothing new to commit."
cd "$ROOT"
git add -- "${DATA[@]}" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
if ! git diff --cached --quiet -- "${DATA[@]}"; then
    if git commit -q -m "Weekly forecast capture $TODAY ($(ls "$SNAP" | grep -c "^${TODAY}_[a-z-]*\\.csv$") teams)" -m "Automated by scripts/scheduled_capture.sh (launchd com.keystone.forecastcapture)." -- "${DATA[@]}" >> "$LOG" 2>&1; then
        if push_bg; then git_note="Pushed to GitHub."; else git_note="Committed, but the push FAILED."; alert "push failed"; fi
    else
        git_note="Git commit FAILED."; alert "commit failed"
    fi
fi
echo "git: $git_note" >> "$LOG"
'''
assert old_run in s; s=s.replace(old_run,new_run)
s=s.replace('teams=$(ls "$SNAP" | grep -c "^${TODAY}_")','teams=$(ls "$SNAP" | grep -c "^${TODAY}_[a-z-]*\\.csv$")')
for a,b in [('No action needed. Ask Claude','No action needed. $git_note Ask Claude'),

            ('Action: ask Claude for /forecast-capture step 5."','Action: ask Claude for /forecast-capture step 5. $git_note"')]:
    assert a in s; s=s.replace(a,b)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
